concepts.why: The patient's symptoms of postprandial upper abdominal pain, intractable vomiting, and bloating, combined with the finding of compression of the third portion of the duodenum between the superior mesenteric artery and the aorta at an acute angle, are consistent with Superior Mesenteric Artery Syndrome.
The patient's symptoms of gastric distension, nausea, and vomiting, combined with the normal upper gastrointestinal endoscopy, are consistent with Gastroparesis.
The patient's symptoms of obstructive symptoms, abdominal pain, and vomiting, combined with the finding of compression of the third portion of the duodenum, are consistent with Duodenal obstruction.
It explains the finding of no intrinsic luminal lesions in the context of duodenal obstruction.

rationales.F01: Intractable vomiting is a common symptom of Superior Mesenteric Artery Syndrome and Extrinsic Duodenal Compression.
rationales.F07: Compression of the third portion of the duodenum between the superior mesenteric artery and the aorta at an acute angle is a characteristic finding of Superior Mesenteric Artery Syndrome and Extrinsic Duodenal Compression.
rationales.F04: Being markedly lean may contribute to the development of Superior Mesenteric Artery Syndrome.
rationales.F06: Marked gastric distension can be a consequence of duodenal obstruction, which is consistent with Superior Mesenteric Artery Syndrome, Extrinsic Duodenal Compression, and Duodenal obstruction.
